name: Nifuroxazide

overview.mechanism: ANSM describes nifuroxazide as an intestinal antiseptic; this does not establish clinical benefit for viral diarrhea [[NIFANSM]].
uses: French 2019 regulator information limits the indication to presumed bacterial acute diarrhea without suspected invasive features; exact Philippine Entefuryl labeling must be checked [[NIFANSM,PHREG]].

sources.citation: FDA Philippines product-registration data preserved in the website registry; exact generic/product records inspected November 25, 2026. Cached record, not a new verification of current registration validity.

ANSM. Nifuroxazide(ERCEFURYL and generics): prescription requirement and contraindication below 18 years. Healthcare-professional safety communication, July 2019. Verified November 25, 2026. French restrictions, not represented as Philippine approval text.
Begovic B, et al. Open Clinical Trial on Using Nifuroxazide Compared to Probiotics in Treating Acute Diarrhoeas in Adults. Mater Sociomed.2016; 28(6):454–458. PMID 28144199.

draft_notes: No inferred CKD-band, HD, PD or CRRT regimen. Current Philippine product identity/insert governs applicability.

revision_log.change: Source-verified descriptive evidence and explicitly attributed regulatory guidance; numerical recommended doses only from verified exact local insert.
revision_log.approved_by: W. G. M. Rivero, MD (delegated source-verification workflow; executed by Codex, 2026-11-25)

usual_adult_dose.dose: No numerical regimen assigned: the 200 mg capsule registry record does not establish approved dose or duration. Research regimens are not prescribing instructions [[PHREG,NIFOBS]]

contraindications: French 2019 restriction: contraindicated in children/adolescents under 18 years. This is attributed foreign safety information, not a verified Philippine contraindication list [[NIFANSM]]

serious: ANSM reported very rare but sometimes severe immune-allergic reactions, including anaphylactic shock and angioedema [[NIFANSM]]

monitoring: Fever, systemic illness or other suspected invasive features fall outside the French regulator-described indication. ANSM emphasizes that most diarrhea resolves without medication and that oral rehydration is central in young children [[NIFANSM]]

evidence.title: Evidence quality and kidney limitations
evidence.intro: No renal dose band, HD, PD or CRRT regimen is established here; lack of data is not evidence that diarrhea or treatment is harmless in kidney disease.

rows.findings: No exact local insert verified in this review.
rows.limitations: French restriction is a safety comparator, not a replacement for Philippine product instructions.

rows.design: Open prospective observational study; 169 adults; not described as randomized in its abstract.
rows.intervention: Nifuroxazide versus a lactic-acid-bacteria probiotic for acute diarrhea.
rows.findings: Reported mean time to last unformed stool 2 days versus 5 days(P=0.0001); reported safety/tolerability similar.
rows.limitations: No blinded placebo comparison; potential selection/confounding and manufacturer-affiliated authors. Does not establish routine benefit in viral diarrhea, severe/invasive illness, children or renal failure.

rows.findings: Prescription-only restriction and age contraindication followed limited pediatric evidence and serious immune-allergic reports; no demonstrated clinical value for viral infectious diarrhea.
rows.limitations: Historical foreign regulatory action; current local prescribing details remain unverified.

renal: The cited adult observational diarrhea study does not establish dosing or safety in kidney failure, HD, PD or CRRT; no renal schedule is inferred [[NIFOBS]].
An exact Philippine Entefuryl renal instruction was not verified. This evidence gap must not be presented as proof that adjustment or kidney-related monitoring is unnecessary [[PHREG,NIFOBS]].
